news.title: The 2026 World Cup proved that planned mega-event expansion is unsustainable
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup was sold as football’s biggest celebration yet. By the time Spain lifted the trophy in New Jersey after dismantling Argentina in a one-sided final, it had certainly delivered on scale. One-hundred-and-four matches. Six weeks of football stretched across an entire continent.

news.title: Cape Verde World Cup hero Vozinha agrees move to Chile's Colo Colo
news.lede: July 24 : Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, who emerged as one of the World Cup's biggest surprise packages, has reached an agreement to join Chilean side Colo Colo, club president Anibal Mosa said on Friday. The 40-year-old free agent will travel to Chile to undergo a medical before being officially unveiled at the Estadio Monumental, Mosa told reporters ahead of Colo Colo's league match against Deportes Limache. "Vozinha will be a Colo Colo player. In the coming days he will travel to Chile, undergo the usual medical examinations and then be presented here at the Estadio Monumental," Mosa said.

news.title: Bayern Munich star Michael Olise plays in NYC pickup game
news.lede: You have to give it to Bayern Munich and France superstar Michael Olise, the man does love football. Well, after France lost the third-place game at the World Cup to England, the 24-year-old could not stay away from the game for long, so he joined a pickup game in New York City. Imagine you are stretching trying to get loose after sitting in a cube all day pouring through spreadsheets and you look across the field and have to defend Olise. Not just Olise, though, but Olise wearing some wild pants.

news.title: Cape Verde's World Cup hero Vozinha finds new club; it's not Lionel Messi's Inter Miami
news.lede: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha has found a new club after his memorable FIFA World Cup campaign, signing for Colo Colo as a free agent. The move ends weeks of speculation linking the veteran shot-stopper with Lionel Messi's Inter Miami during the summer transfer window.The 40-year-old was without a club after leaving Portuguese side Chaves on July 1. Following his standout performances at the World Cup, rumours suggested an MLS switch could be on the cards, with Inter Miami among the clubs reportedly interested. Instead, Vozinha has chosen to continue his career with Colo Colo, who announced the signing with the caption 'AURA' embedded in the announcement post on social media.

news.title: Lionel Messi quietly made Vozinha's family's World Cup dream come true before final
news.lede: Lionel Messi reportedly ensured that four members of Cabo Verde goalkeeper Vozinha's family could attend the 2026 FIFA World Cup final after arranging tickets for them at his own expense. The gesture took place before Argentina's title clash against Spain at the New York New Jersey Stadium, where Messi's side suffered a 1-0 defeat after extra time. The story only emerged after the final, with Messi having made no public mention of his involvement. Argentine journalist Yanina Latorre revealed that Messi purchased a large number of tickets during the tournament for people who could not afford to attend matches.

news.title: How World Cup 2026 proved football has remarkable ability to cure all ills
news.lede: The trophy safely on display at the Spanish FA headquarters, England’s wounds no longer so raw, and the annual football calendar now into its miniscule vacuum, you’re left to reflect on the past six weeks and ponder whether the 2026 edition in the United States, Canada and Mexico was a resounding success or an unmitigated flop. This one really could have gone either way. The expansion from 32 teams to 48 had the potential for greater drama but also the risk of suffocating, of making the World Cup the one thing it should never be: tedious. Would North America buy into soccer in a way we hadn’t seen at USA 1994?
